expense-extract.title: Alex's customer rollout expenses
expense-extract.text: FICTIONAL DEMO. Choose Quick start for 3 receipts, Customer rollout for 9, or Needs review for deliberate exceptions. Preview any receipt below the picker, then press Start. Keep EUR and USD totals separate and check the refund's minus sign. First run may download models. The answer key is fixture truth, not measured model output.

doc-qa.title: Prepare the September 17 go/no-go
doc-qa.text: FICTIONAL DEMO. Choose a question, press Index folder, then Ask. The six documents connect customer obligations, field evidence, release decisions and money. Follow up with: Which date superseded June 30, and does that affect Lyon? Expected: October 19 cold-storage target, outside Lyon scope. Do not invent a broad GA date.

html-creator.title: From operating documents to a client-ready brief
html-creator.text: FICTIONAL DEMO. Choose the Meridian customer launch brief for a grounded report, the pilot control room for a dashboard, or Atelier Quay for a hospitality page. Press Generate. Inspect conditional dates and separate currencies. Generated pages should retain the fictional-demo label and use no external assets.

code-review-assist.title: Review a plausible release candidate
code-review-assist.text: FICTIONAL DEMO CODE. Pick Customer export or Dock C fix, then Review. The sample automatically selects pasted-diff mode. Neither diff is applied or executed. Discuss concrete defects and missing tests rather than asking for generic code quality.

screen-ocr.title: Read the original receipt
screen-ocr.text: FICTIONAL DEMO. Choose a hotel folio, cafe receipt or credit note and press Extract text. No file picker is needed. Compare the OCR text with the local preview. Pay attention to decimal commas, line-item totals and a negative refund. Try the same files in Expense Report Extractor to compare raw OCR with structured output.

live-translation.title: Customer handover · French to English
live-translation.text: FICTIONAL READ-ALOUD SCRIPT. Select your microphone, press Start, then read: Bonjour, voici le point sur notre projet fictif à Lyon. La visite de septembre a permis de terminer cinquante-sept missions sur soixante. Le lancement du vingt et un septembre reste conditionnel. Sofia doit corriger la carte avant le douze septembre. Marcus terminera les tests le seize. Priya prendra la décision finale le dix-sept. Le client a payé un acompte de douze mille euros. Le solde dépend de la réception du pilote. Stop when finished. Compare dates, names and payment conditions; there is no prerecorded result.

meeting-notes.title: 90-second project stand-up
meeting-notes.text: FICTIONAL READ-ALOUD MEETING. Choose microphone capture and Start. Read with pauses: Alex: The Lyon workshop is finished. Fifty-seven of sixty missions succeeded without intervention. One controlled stop occurred at Dock C, with no collision or injury. Sofia: I own the map-validation fix. It is due September twelfth, but it is not released yet. Marcus: I need the fix before I can complete two hundred regression scenarios by September sixteenth. Elise: I will send the revised aisle plan by September eleventh. Priya: I will make the go or no-go decision on September seventeenth. September twenty-first remains a conditional installation date. Dana: We received twelve thousand euros, not the full forty-eight-thousand-euro contract. Keep the dollar subscription separate from euro travel. Alex: I will publish the operator checklist by September fifteenth. Stop capture and generate notes. Check that owners, dates, dependencies and the open decision survive.

voice-assistant.title: A practical briefing assistant
voice-assistant.text: FICTIONAL DEMO PROMPTS. Start with your chosen wake word. Say: Help me rewrite this customer update in two clear sentences: our fictional Lyon pilot is planned for September twenty-first, but Priya must approve it on September seventeenth after QA passes. Then ask: What three questions should I ask before confirming the trip? Supply these facts aloud; the voice assistant has not automatically ingested the document pack. Stop after the demonstration.

voice-clone-studio.title: An operational announcement in your own voice
voice-clone-studio.text: FICTIONAL DEMO. Enroll a short sample of your own voice, choose a script and synthesize. The prompts cover a customer handover, an executive briefing and a hotel welcome. No real person's voice or third-party voice recording is bundled. Listen for clarity around names, dates and monetary amounts.

smart-recall.title: Find the briefing you just saw
smart-recall.text: FICTIONAL CONTENT; recording captures the actual selected screen. Open the demo briefing link, start recording only when ready, keep that page visible until an indexed event appears, then stop. Return and choose a search prompt. Results depend on what was actually captured, not a prebuilt fake index. Avoid displaying unrelated private content while recording.

object-detection.title: A live desk-side inventory
object-detection.text: DEMO SCENARIO. This brick uses live camera/screen input, not fabricated detection results. Place an ordinary bottle, cup and book on a clear desk, choose the source and Start. Move one object at a time and compare detections. No fake photo is supplied: simple drawn silhouettes would give a misleading accuracy demonstration. Stop capture when finished.

webcam-effects.title: A fictional customer video briefing
webcam-effects.text: DEMO SCENARIO. Choose camera and a supported engine, then Start. Use a plain background and switch Blur / Replace while framing yourself as a presenter of the fictional Meridian pilot. GPU/AUTO remain gated until numerical qualification. This uses your live camera; no third-party face or prerecorded effect is supplied. Stop when finished.

smart-city-monitor.title: Interpret track counts honestly
smart-city-monitor.text: DEMO SCENARIO. Existing city-camera presets are REAL external network feeds, not fictional sample files. Select a feed or your own local clip and Start. Counts are experimental new tracks, not unique people or vehicles; lost tracks can be counted again. No synthetic traffic clip or guaranteed counts are claimed by this sample refresh. Use the visible labels when presenting results.
